h: Keeping little astronauts busy around Loch Leven
p: While Aero Space builds towards its big launch, Kinross has plenty to keep space-mad kids and their grown-ups entertained. The obvious starting point is Loch Leven itself. A heritage trail loops right around the water, flat and family-friendly, so you can walk a chunk of it or hire bikes and tackle more of the circuit. It's a lovely, open stretch of countryside with big skies, which is exactly what budding astronomers need.

Out on an island in the loch sits Loch Leven Castle, where Mary, Queen of Scots was held prisoner before her famous escape in 1568. In the warmer months a boat has traditionally carried visitors out to the island, which feels like a proper adventure for children. Bird lovers should look out for the RSPB reserve on the southern shore, where huge flocks of geese gather in autumn and winter.

You don't need to wait for a finished building to start stargazing, either. Away from the brighter lights of the cities, the countryside around Kinross can offer decent dark skies on a clear winter night. Wrap up warm, give your eyes twenty minutes to adjust, and see how many constellations you can pick out. A free star-map app on your phone helps, though switch it to night mode so you don't ruin everyone's eyesight.
Then, when a Cosmos Planetarium session pops up nearby, the kids will already know what they're looking at.
